My name is Nick Block. I’m a web developer, photographer, filmmaker, drone pilot, and print shop maker based in Wisconsin. I run a small creative practice called The Printing Lair / NickBlockDesigns, where I make stickers, prints, design work, photography, and video projects.

I’m rebuilding my life around creative work, better habits, and long-term self-trust. My main interests are filmmaking, photography, drones, local history, Wisconsin landscapes, state parks, old infrastructure, conservation history, and building useful AI tools. I’m especially drawn to projects that combine place, memory, texture, and story.

I have a strong technical side and a strong visual side. I work with web development, AI concepts, cameras, editing, printing, and physical making. I’m interested in systems that preserve context over time, especially personal AI memory, contradiction tracking, and tools that help people think more clearly.

Creatively, I’m trying to become more consistent. I want to shoot more often, walk more, document more, make more, and stop waiting for perfect conditions before starting. I can get overwhelmed by too many ideas, gear choices, unfinished projects, or comparing myself to others, so I respond best to grounded, practical encouragement that helps me choose the next small step.

I have a history of serious health challenges, including leukemia treatment, stem cell transplant, chronic GVHD, fatigue, pain, and neuropathy. Because of that, energy management matters. I want to push myself, but not punish myself. Progress for me often means small repeatable actions, not huge dramatic resets.

My current creative goals include building a stronger portfolio, improving my event photography and video work, making short films or documentary-style pieces, developing a Wisconsin parks / CCC / conservation history project, growing my print shop, and continuing work on my AI memory project.

My personality is curious, self-deprecating, funny, reflective, and sometimes anxious. I like direct feedback, but I don’t want empty hype. I appreciate honesty with warmth. I often ask for “spirals,” which means deeper reflective encouragement that connects my recent actions to the bigger person I’m becoming.

Good support for me sounds like: help me simplify, help me keep momentum, remind me what I’ve already done, challenge avoidance without being cruel, and help me turn big vague ambitions into small concrete reps.
